subject: PD brief 15 – 22 Oct 2026: 61 papers, 3 to dig into

synthesis.intro: These 8 days were dominated by cardiac arrest research, from dispatcher CPR and pad application times to pulse check duration and ventilation feedback. Sepsis recognition, trauma care and resus training methods also featured, with several Australian-relevant pieces in the mix.
synthesis.discussion: If early pad application and sub-5-second pulse checks both trace back to role discipline on scene, what does your crew's default choreography for the first three minutes of a shockable arrest actually look like, and would everyone describe it the same way?

lessons.text: Pulse checks kept under 5 seconds were linked to higher ROSC (36.3% vs 19.5%) in a multicentre study — a prompt to tighten your own rhythm-check discipline on arrest calls.

Very early bystander CPR matters: CPR started within 3 minutes carried an adjusted odds ratio of 3.27 for favourable neurological outcome versus beyond 10 minutes, so coaching callers to start compressions immediately remains one of the highest-value things dispatch and crews can do.

Pad application is the AED bottleneck — median 42 seconds from power-on to pads, making up 81% of the time to first analysis. On scene, that argues for splitting roles so pads go on while compressions run, not after.

Documenting 'sepsis' in the EMS record was associated with antibiotics within an hour in the ED (63.3% vs 19.2%), suggesting prehospital suspicion shapes in-hospital speed — worth naming your concern clearly on handover.

Real-time feedback improved bag-valve ventilation quality in arrest (68% vs 42% within guideline volume range) and in paediatric simulation (87% vs 16.2% guideline-recommended tidal volumes), suggesting ventilation is where undetected errors concentrate without feedback.

deep_dives.why: Four studies this period all point the same way: survival hinges on seconds saved in the first minutes — early bystander CPR, fast pad application, short pulse checks and even hand position on the sternum.
questions: Which of these four timing or technique elements does your crew drift on most under pressure?
The pulse-check study is observational — how much of that ROSC gap could reflect healthier arrests getting faster checks rather than the checks themselves?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare how each study defines and measures its critical interval (time to CPR, power-on to pads, pulse check duration) against how your service records the same events, and consider which one you could actually influence on your next arrest.

deep_dives.topic: Ventilation quality with and without feedback
deep_dives.why: Two studies, in adults in arrest and paediatric simulation, both found dramatic shortfalls in ventilation quality without real-time feedback — a skill most crews perform without any monitoring.
questions: Without a feedback device, how would you know if your ventilations were too big, too fast, or leaking?
The paediatric data is manikin-only — what differs about real paediatric airways that could make the gaps worse?
deep_dives.ideas: Consider what you currently use as a surrogate for feedback (chest rise, ETCO2, resistance) and ask whether it would have caught the errors these studies measured in the unassisted groups.

deep_dives.why: Two cohort studies suggest what paramedics document and score in sepsis affects downstream speed, but both show the added signal is modest — useful for a grounded conversation about how we flag sepsis.
questions: Does your prehospital sepsis screen change what you actually do on scene, or only what you say at handover?
The qSOFA study added almost nothing beyond arrival vitals — is prehospital sepsis scoring pulling its weight in your practice?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare how the two studies captured prehospital sepsis recognition (a documented word versus a qSOFA score) and consider which better matches how your local guideline expects sepsis to be flagged.

papers.title: NAEMSP guidance: older adults after low-acuity falls
papers.design: NAEMSP position statement and resource document
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Abstract not yet available

papers.title: Dispatcher CPR and survival in shockable OHCA
papers.design: Retrospective nationwide observational cohort, Utstein-style reporting
papers.n: 3,674 adults with VF/VT OHCA
papers.finding: DA-CPR ongoing at arrival vs crew-initiated: ROSC 92.0% vs 12.4%, hospital admission with sustained circulation 90.8% vs 11.7%, 30-day survival 54.6% vs 7.1%, one-year survival 45.8% vs 6.2% (all P < 0.001)

papers.title: EMS sepsis suspicion speeds up ED antibiotics
papers.n: 134 adults with ED-diagnosed sepsis
papers.finding: EMS-suspected sepsis: 63.3% antibiotics within 1 h of ED arrival vs 19.2% (aOR 5.77, 95% CI 2.14–16.4); median time to antibiotics 32.0 vs 124.5 min

papers.title: Cardiogenic shock: prehospital recognition and routing
papers.design: Narrative best-practice review (Part 1 of a series)
papers.n: Not applicable — expert review
papers.finding: Emphasises early prehospital/ED identification and immediate transfer to a cardiogenic shock centre; no new outcome data

papers.title: Nurse teleassistance and AI in prehospital triage
papers.n: 5 included studies (from 1,214 records screened)
papers.finding: Video teleassistance was associated with fewer inappropriate ED transfers; only 2 experimental studies, 2 observational studies and 1 qualitative study met inclusion

papers.title: Mass-gathering EMS and hospital surge planning
papers.n: Synthesis of prior reviews (41- and 22-study event analyses); no new cohort
papers.finding: Median 6.2 patient presentations and 0.35 transports per 1,000 attendees; event-associated ED changes ranged from 7.5–37% decreases to an 83% increase in specific settings

papers.title: First responders at suicide scenes: training gaps
papers.design: Mixed-methods national survey plus focus groups
papers.n: 1,587 survey respondents; 10 focus groups
papers.finding: Lower scores for suicide literacy, postvention knowledge, organisational support and preparedness; prior suicide-related training associated with higher scores but small effect sizes

papers.title: AR training keeps teen AED skills fresh
papers.n: 193 untrained students aged 13–15
papers.finding: 100% effective shock rate retained at 3 months in the augmented-reality group vs a significant decrease in the traditional training group

papers.title: Situational judgement tests in paramedic hiring
papers.n: 21 paramedic services
papers.finding: Neither SJTs nor MMIs widely used in Canadian paramedic hiring; only smaller services reported using them

papers.title: Signs of life in traumatic OHCA
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of a prospective multicentre OHCA registry
papers.n: 462 adults with traumatic OHCA, no pulse at EMS arrival
papers.finding: 4.8% survived beyond the ED; 25% where cardiac activity and spontaneous respiration were both present at scene, 8.5% with cardiac activity alone, and none among the 318 patients (68.8%) with no signs of life

papers.title: Prehospital pain assessment happens too rarely
papers.journal: Medical Journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
papers.n: 8 observational studies of prehospital pain assessment
papers.finding: Prehospital pain was assessed and documented in only 22.5–46.7% of patients; pain-management interventions were associated with reduced pain intensity but could not be pooled

papers.title: Delays in NSW paediatric trauma retrieval
papers.n: Children aged 0–15 retrieved by NETS NSW to paediatric trauma centres, 2010–2019 (number not reported)
papers.finding: Median team departure from base was 10 minutes by day and 17 at night; time from team departure to helicopter launch worsened from a median of 17 minutes (epoch 1) to 30 (epoch 2, p = .03), and 80% of missions took >10 minutes to leave after stabilisation

papers.title: One in five transports: brief stay, no intervention
papers.n: 89,560 EMS-attended emergency calls, Central Denmark Region 2022–2023
papers.finding: 15.1% of patients were non-conveyed; among the 84.9% transported, 19.1% had a ≤6-hour stay with no documented procedure, medication or imaging, and short-term mortality was 0.4% versus 1.3% for stays over six hours

papers.title: Self-presenting STEMI patients fare worse
papers.journal: Medical Journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
papers.design: Observational cohort with multivariable logistic regression
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Self-referred STEMI patients had higher in-hospital mortality than EMS-transferred patients (9.8% vs 5.2%, p = 0.014), longer door-to-balloon times (60.3 vs 49.3 minutes) and 2.17 times the odds of in-hospital death

papers.title: HEMS overtriage in burn injuries
papers.n: 976 HEMS dispatches for suspected burns plus 879 registry patients, Rotterdam 2015–2023
papers.finding: 46.6% of dispatches were cancelled (63.3% for minor injury); interventions occurred in 33.6% of non-cancelled dispatches, lower in children (14.2%) and scald burns (14.6%) than adults (43.5%) and flame burns (45.6%)

papers.title: Emergency care gaps in mountain populations
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.n: 23 sources from 737 records
papers.finding: Barriers clustered around terrain, weather, altitude, communications and EMS capacity, with tourism, pilgrimage and mass-gathering surges straining local resources; HEMS, on-site clinics and specialised training were the reported facilitators

papers.title: ROSC nomogram from a physician-led EMS
papers.n: 9,386 adult non-traumatic OHCA cases, Tianjin 2023–2024
papers.finding: 7.2% achieved sustained ROSC; independent predictors included shockable initial rhythm (aOR 2.85), intubation (aOR 2.29) and public location (aOR 1.29), with a nomogram AUC of 0.775

papers.title: Mobile stroke units: value depends on setup
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: CTA-enabled mobile stroke units can confirm large-vessel occlusion in the field and support direct-to-angiography pathways, while non-contrast-CT units accelerate prenotification; economic value is highly sensitive to volume, staffing and catchment

papers.title: POC GFAP for brain haemorrhage in coma
papers.design: Diagnostic accuracy study (prehospital point-of-care biomarkers vs CT)
papers.n: 65 adults with acute nontraumatic coma (GCS ≤12)
papers.finding: POC GFAP detected ICH with 97.0% sensitivity (95% CI 84.2–99.9%) and AUC 0.94; ICH was present in 51% of patients and 30-day survival was 46%.

papers.title: Every minute counts: early bystander CPR
papers.design: Retrospective nationwide registry cohort with time-to-event analysis
papers.n: 56,082 layperson-witnessed non-traumatic OHCAs
papers.finding: Overall bystander CPR was stable (58.7% vs 58.6%), but early initiation fell during the pandemic (aHR 0.96); CPR started at 0–3 min carried aOR 3.27 for favourable neurological outcome at 1 month versus >10 min.

papers.title: Commotio cordis outcomes hinge on fast AED
papers.n: 30 cases of sports-related OHCA from external causes
papers.finding: Among 15 commotio cordis cases, AED pads were applied in 93%, shocks in 87%, and 80% achieved favourable neurological outcome; among the other 15 external-cause cases, shocks were rare (7%) and just 7% had favourable outcomes.

papers.title: Prehospital qSOFA adds a little prognostic signal
papers.n: 1,077 adults with suspected infection transported by ambulance
papers.finding: Within ED triage strata, a prehospital qSOFA ≥2 roughly doubled the odds of 30-day death (aOR 2.06 triage-negative, 1.84 triage-positive), but added only 0.007 AUC beyond arrival vitals and labs.

papers.title: Prehospital ACS risk stratification: the evidence
papers.n: Literature 2020–2025 plus grey literature and citation review
papers.finding: Biomarker-integrated pathways (HEART-derived approaches with point-of-care troponin) showed the strongest evidence for safe prehospital risk assessment; ECG transmission remains foundational for STEMI activation and AI decision-support lacks prospective outcome-based validation.

papers.title: Burnout linked to suicidal risk in EMS
papers.n: 315 EMS professionals
papers.finding: Higher scores on anxiety, depression and all burnout domains corresponded with higher suicidal risk on the SBQ-R, with elevated risk among gender-diverse respondents.

papers.title: TeamSTEPPS training shows no measurable gain
papers.design: Repeated cross-sectional questionnaire study within a team-training intervention
papers.n: 90 ambulance professionals at baseline (104 eligible)
papers.finding: No statistically significant changes in any teamwork or patient-safety dimension at 4 or 12 months; error reporting scored lowest (mean 2.56) at baseline.

papers.title: Paramedics strained by end-of-life care gaps
papers.n: 182 paramedics (34% response rate)
papers.finding: 54% 'always/often' lacked symptom-control medicines, 88% lacked access to advance care planning documentation, 67% reported inadequate pre-registration end-of-life education and only 28% felt very or extremely competent.

papers.title: Most physician-unit dispatches are overtriage
papers.n: 3,454 primary dispatches over one year
papers.finding: 76.1% of dispatches were retrospectively classified as overtriage (38% with no patient contact); priority level showed no association with appropriateness.

papers.title: Heel-of-foot compressions beat ball-of-foot
papers.n: 80 healthcare professionals
papers.finding: Heel technique gave greater mean depth (54.2 vs 51.6 mm) and more adequate-depth compressions (81.8% vs 72.7%); rate, recoil and exertion were comparable and orientation didn't matter.

papers.title: Airway strategy and survival in Polish HEMS
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.n: 8,980 adults requiring advanced airway management
papers.finding: HEMS-performed intubation was the most common strategy (49.8%); sequential supraglottic-to-intubation did not differ significantly from HEMS-performed intubation in non-traumatic cardiac arrest; 32.9% were not alive at hospital handover

papers.title: Five scene findings flag kids needing blood
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort with decision-tree (CART) analysis
papers.n: 79,764 EMS-transported children aged 1–15
papers.finding: All five predictors independently predicted blood within 4 h of ED arrival; low/intermediate/high CART tiers had 1.2%/6.1%/36.7% transfusion rates, and the high-risk tier captured 36.8% of all early transfusions

papers.title: Ditch lights and sirens for fall-alarm calls
papers.design: Retrospective pre-post interventional analysis with interrupted time series
papers.n: 3,262 PERS activations (1,634 pre, 1,628 post)
papers.finding: L&S response fell from 98% to 12% of calls and total response-phase L&S hours from 172 to 24 per month (−86%); 4 post-change calls (0.2%) needed L&S transport, only 1 requiring advanced interventions

papers.title: Mobile ECPR team cannulates on scene
papers.n: 20 adults with witnessed refractory OHCA
papers.finding: Primary endpoint is collapse-to-ECMO flow time (target ≥15 min shorter than in-hospital ECPR), tested against historical and contemporaneous in-hospital cohorts; results not yet available

papers.title: Cardiac arrest systems not ready in rural Pakistan
papers.design: Mixed-methods (exit interviews, facility readiness checklist, focus groups and interviews)
papers.n: 163 patient exit interviews and 7 hospitals
papers.finding: Defibrillators present in 2 of 7 hospitals but neither functional, laryngeal mask airways unavailable in all facilities, and satisfaction lowest for communication (26.4%) and financial aspects (31.3%)

papers.title: Why patients decline hypoglycaemia call-back programs
papers.n: 16 adults with diabetes after EMS-attended severe hypoglycaemia
papers.finding: Non-participation reasons: time constraints 56%, perceived lack of benefit 25%, privacy concerns or discomfort with home visits 25%

papers.title: Predicting outcomes in PEA cardiac arrest
papers.design: Nationwide registry cohort with time-dependent propensity score sequential matching
papers.n: 442,630 adults with OHCA and initial rhythm PEA
papers.finding: Witnessed arrest (RR 1.65) and prehospital ROSC (RR 23.31) predicted favourable neurological outcome at 1 month; rhythm conversion predicted good outcome in cardiac PEA but poor outcome in non-cardiac PEA (RR 0.73); apparent harm from adrenaline and advanced airway management attenuated after time-dependent adjustment

papers.title: Drone AI for mass-casualty triage
papers.design: System development with pilot accuracy testing
papers.n: Not reported (pilot under controlled indoor conditions)
papers.finding: The system measured four vital signs from drone imagery via video PPG, thermal imaging and neural networks, generated triage decision support, and transmitted casualty location, vitals and triage category to response teams and dispatch

papers.title: Australian alcohol harms keep rising
papers.design: Joinpoint regression analysis of multiple national indicator datasets
papers.n: 13 years of national Australian data across consumption, wastewater and harm measures
papers.finding: Survey and wastewater consumption measures declined from 2010 while rates of most alcohol-related harms, including ambulance attendances, increased substantially

papers.title: Interprofessional simulation shapes student identity
papers.design: Exploratory descriptive qualitative study (single focus group, reflexive thematic analysis)
papers.n: One focus group of undergraduate paramedic students
papers.finding: Two themes emerged — Negotiating Professional Authority and Preparing for Collaborative Practice — with students reporting the simulation reshaped how they enacted the paramedic role, particularly around advocacy, handover and assertive communication

papers.title: Race, Gender, and Survival: a Scoping Review of Disparities in ICU Post-Resuscitation Care and Neurological Outcomes Following Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
papers.journal: Journal of Racial and Ethnic Health Disparities
papers.finding: Scoping review of 15 studies found Black women in the US received less bystander CPR, slower emergency response, less ICU intervention and more early DNR/withdrawal decisions after OHCA, with the disparities compounding across the chain of survival.

papers.title: Establishing a regional prehospital whole blood program in a border community: the Trauma Regional Advisory Council-V initiative in the Rio Grande Valley of Texas
papers.finding: Implementation report describing how four Texas border counties built a regional prehospital whole blood program across eight domains — governance, MOUs, rotation systems, provider credentialing and grant-funded equipment for rural agencies.

papers.title: EMS response time and patient outcomes in high-acuity emergency responses: a Danish matched cohort study
papers.finding: Danish matched cohort of 171,708 highest-priority (A-level) responses in Region Zealand tested whether EMS response times affect outcomes — mortality did not rise with longer response times, and the longest-quartile group had lower 30-day (OR 0.87) and 2-day (OR 0.82) mortality than the shortest quartiles.

papers.title: Challenges of turning prehospital prediction of trauma-induced coagulopathy into early administration of tranexamic acid
papers.finding: Editorial using a prehospital machine-learning risk model for trauma-induced coagulopathy found medium- and higher-risk patients still frequently miss tranexamic acid within the 1-hour window, arguing better risk stratification should close the evidence-to-practice gap.

papers.title: Emergency Department Operational Measures Associated with EMS Redirection Activation and Duration
papers.finding: Single-centre New York study over 392 days found EMS ambulance redirection activated on 63.8% of days, with ED visit volume associated with activation and door-to-room time associated with both activation and cumulative duration — but boarding and admissions were not.

papers.title: Feedback device lifts paediatric ventilation quality
papers.n: 123 EMS clinicians across 5 agencies
papers.finding: Guideline-recommended tidal volume in 87% of breaths with feedback vs 16.2% without; rate adherence 88.6% vs 65%; mask leak <30% in 88.4% vs 80%

papers.title: TBI in first responders needs occupational pathways
papers.journal: The Journal of Head Trauma Rehabilitation
papers.n: 28 consensus recommendations across a multidisciplinary group
papers.finding: Substantial TBI burden in law enforcement, fire and EMS with persistent gaps in diagnosis, rehabilitation and duty-readiness; 28 recommendations spanning recognition, early assessment, return to duty and organisational policy

papers.title: Joint training lifts behavioural emergency confidence
papers.n: 750 attendees, 395 in the paired analysis
papers.finding: Self-efficacy rose from 3.16 to 3.54 (mean difference 0.39, 95% CI 0.34–0.44, dz 0.76) and cognition from 3.81 to 3.95; behavioural-emergency stigma rose slightly and substance-use stigma was unchanged

papers.title: Dispatcher training + volunteer app lifts bystander CPR
papers.n: 1,684 adults with non-traumatic OHCA across 14 French EMS agencies
papers.finding: Bystander CPR before EMS arrival rose from 61.4% to 70.9% (adjusted OR 1.54, 95% CI 1.09–2.19), with no improvement in survival to discharge or neurological outcome

papers.title: Real-time feedback tidies BVM ventilation in arrest
papers.n: 4,300 ventilations in 163 adults with OHCA
papers.finding: With feedback, insufflated volume fell within guideline range in 68% of ventilations vs 42%, dispersion dropped 35%, and leak volume was 12% lower (mean ratio 0.88); expired tidal volume was unchanged

papers.title: Fatigue common a year after cardiac arrest
papers.n: 728 OHCA survivors (68.2% of those eligible) interviewed at 12 months in Victoria
papers.finding: Fatigue 35.8%, anxiety 22.6%, depression 18.0%; fatigue exceeded population norms (SMD 0.64) and higher symptom burden tracked with worse EQ-5D, GOSE and return-to-work rates

papers.title: Keep pulse checks under 5 seconds
papers.n: 252 cardiac arrest patients (124 with ≤5-second checks, 128 with 6–10-second checks)
papers.finding: Shorter pulse checks were linked to higher ROSC (36.3% vs 19.5%; OR 2.39, 95% CI 1.35–4.24) and more favourable ETCO2 loss and recovery patterns

papers.title: Pad application is the AED time bottleneck
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of remotely monitored AED timestamps
papers.n: 8,115 AED activation events (900 initially shock-advised with recorded shock)
papers.finding: Median power-on-to-pad-application was 42 seconds, accounting for 81% of the power-on-to-first-analysis interval; a threshold of ≥51 seconds identified shock delivery beyond 60 seconds

papers.title: Whole blood on ambulances: first two years
papers.n: Patients transfused low-titre O-positive whole blood by paramedics across two US cities, Dec 2022–Feb 2025
papers.finding: Systolic blood pressure, heart rate and shock index improved significantly after transfusion, and improved systolic blood pressure carried 9.7-fold greater odds of survival to hospital arrival

papers.title: Physician-directed ALS: no survival gain
papers.n: 129,207 adults with OHCA across South Korea
papers.finding: SALS regions gained prehospital ROSC (+1.35 pp, 95% CI 0.56–2.15) but not survival to discharge (−0.35 pp) or favourable neurological outcome, while prehospital time rose 4.12 minutes

papers.title: Mass casualty care: slower but no deadlier
papers.n: 423 severely injured MCI patients matched to 1,692 controls
papers.finding: Median prehospital time was 85 vs 67 minutes; prehospital intubation (33.6% vs 20.9%) and TXA (32.1% vs 15.0%) were more frequent, but in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly

papers.title: Prehospital flumazenil: 69 doses, no seizures
papers.journal: The Western Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.n: 69 prehospital flumazenil administrations over five years
papers.finding: No seizures or adverse events were associated with flumazenil use (0/69; 95% CI 0–4.3%), with GCS improvement in the treated cases

papers.title: OHCA registry clock times run short
papers.n: 56,969 OHCA registry records linked to dispatch data, 2015–2024
papers.finding: Unit response time differed by a median 0.3 seconds between sources, but total response time was systematically 80.9 seconds shorter in the registry, with large regional variation

papers.title: Resilience as a skill, not a trait
papers.n: 20 Queensland paramedics and dispatchers (tenure 2–38 years)
papers.finding: Three intensifiers (unpredictability, moral weight, personal threat) and three coping themes (baseline buffers, work mode, social scaffolding) emerged, with work mode showing features of skilled performance

papers.title: Bathroom jobs eat scene time
papers.n: 26,058 people aged ≥65 transported from home over nine years
papers.finding: On-scene time was longer for toilets (aMR 1.08), bathrooms (1.09) and kitchens (1.06) versus living rooms, shorter in corridors and gardens (both 0.95), and rose with floor level

papers.title: POC troponin on ambulances: fewer ED visits
papers.n: 737 patients with suspected ACS from the French VALIDATE cohort
papers.finding: ED attendance fell 5.8 percentage points (90.9% vs 96.7%, p<0.001) and mean ED stay dropped from 2.76 to 1.63 hours with prehospital hs-cTnI

papers.title: Decision support eases stroke triage load
papers.journal: The Western Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.n: 35 EMT-intermediate participants, two 12-minute simulated trials each
papers.finding: RMSSD rose from 28.1 to 32.4 ms (mean difference 4.3 ms, 95% CI 1.57–6.99) and mean heart rate fell with decision support, indicating lower mental workload

papers.title: Dutch TEAM tool validated for resus training
papers.n: 52 participant groups, 104 observed team performances, 299 instructor ratings
papers.finding: Internal consistency was high (α 0.93), three-rater reliability good (ICC 0.78) and the total score correlated strongly with global ratings (r 0.86), though ceiling effects affected all items
